title: Nostra Aetate and religious freedom
hookLine: the Church rejects blaming the Jewish people for Christ's death and affirms religious freedom (Dignitatis Humanae)

lines: AN OLD WRONG, A NEW TEACHING.
cards: In our time. That's all the Latin title means: Nostra Aetate. Two plain words to open a short text in which the council asks how Catholics should speak about other religions, and, in one section, about Jews.
Beside it the council set another text, on religious freedom, called Dignitatis Humanae, the dignity of the human person. One looks at an old wrong. The other looks at every conscience.

teach.b: Start with Nostra Aetate. In its section on the Jewish people, the council remembers the spiritual bond that ties the Church to Abraham's descendants.
It says that what happened in Christ's passion cannot be charged against all the Jews living then, without distinction, nor against the Jews of today.
It says the Jews must not be presented as rejected or accursed by God, as if scripture taught that.
And it says the Church deplores hatred, persecution and displays of antisemitism directed against Jews at any time and by anyone.

It grounds this in Saint Paul, who wrote of the Jewish people, in the Douay-Rheims: "For the gifts and the calling of God are without repentance." The council reads it to mean God does not take his gifts back.
Then, Dignitatis Humanae. Its claim fits in a sentence.
Every human person has a right to religious freedom.
No one may be forced to act against their conscience in religious matters, and no one may be stopped from acting by it, within just limits, alone or with others.
The council roots this not in politics but in the dignity of the person, and adds a point from inside the faith itself: the act of faith has to be free. Nobody can be forced into believing.
Both documents ask Catholics to look honestly at the past and to treat every neighbor, of any faith or none, as a person whose conscience is their own.
Catholics have kept working out what these texts mean, in study and in dialogue.

how: Catholic dioceses and the Holy See hold ongoing dialogue with Jewish communities, Catholic teaching rejects antisemitism and any blame of the Jewish people for Christ's death, and the Church teaches that faith must be freely accepted.

the gifts and calling of God

Nostra Aetate says it cannot be charged against all Jews then living, nor against Jews today.
the council deplored antisemitism at any time and by anyone

games.q: you're drafting the council's words about the Jewish people. old sermons blamed them for the passion. what do you write?
o: say nothing and let the old sermons stand.
say the passion cannot be charged against all Jews then or now.
leave it to each preacher to decide.
games.why: Nostra Aetate says Christ's passion cannot be charged against all Jews then living, nor against Jews today, and deplores antisemitism.

practice: Bring to mind a Jewish person or community you know, a synagogue you pass, or simply the Jewish people around the world, and hold them with good will: their safety, their families, their Sabbath, their joy.
If you pray, ask God to bless them and to guard them from hatred. If you don't, simply wish them well, and mean it.

wordCard.voice: Nostra Aetate. The council's rejection of blaming the Jewish people for Christ's death, read alongside its teaching that every conscience is free. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin, in our time: the document's first words, which became its name.

carryVoice: Your line: no one may be forced. Faith, to be faith, has to be free. Day seven hundred ninety-five.
